counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of dense sclerotic bone typical of osteoma
No evidence of a purely fatty lesion without trabecular preservation
No evidence of cortical destruction or aggressive features
decisive_items: sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge, without disruption of the inner or outer tables
The hyperintense foci on T1 images were presumed to represent bone marrow fat
preserved trabecular architecture suggested that pre-existing structures were not destroyed
response.rationale: R2 (hemangioma) is the only candidate that fully integrates the raw spans: a diploic mass with preserved trabeculae, fat-containing T1 hyperintense foci, and intact tables. R5 (osteoma) is contradicted by the presence of fat and preserved trabeculae, as osteomas are dense and lack marrow fat. R1 (lipoma) is contradicted by the trabecular architecture and bony location, which are not features of a simple lipoma.

rejected.why: Lipoma would not show preserved trabeculae or a diploic location with bony bulge; the fat foci are better explained as marrow fat within a hemangioma.
Osteoma is a dense cortical bone lesion without fat foci or preserved trabeculae; the raw spans describe a non-sclerotic, trabecular mass.
